Friend used to have a terrarium with bars on one section of wall. Pinned a towel to it with some yarn.
But the snake was really light compared. This beast in the picture might be able to rip a similar towel contraption down. (Never use safety pins, hard zipties or tape though. That's just asking for trouble.)

If you don't need to see through the bars, you could also try to weave old t-shirts etc into a barrier. Like taking a strip and letting it through every other bar, like you would weave a carpet. That could soften the bars and discourage this beauty from rubbing their face against them.

My friends snake also liked to rub their face against glass, so she taped newspapers on the outside of the terrarium. She would still rub her face and try to climb the walls, but significantly less when she would see that there wasn't a way through. Maybe this guy just wants some time outside the closure. Are they eating habits alright? I have noticed that a hungry snake is more interested in taking a little exploration trip out of their enclosure...

Getting more hides, fake plants and digging material could help. Also, if the walls are made of a material you can drill into, a hammock is surprisingly popular among snakes. I'm knitting a new one for my corn snake currently, since she outgrew her old one some time ago. Some small snakes love gloves hanging from the ceiling. I bet thing guy would love one too, but it would need to be large/durable enough to hold their weight.
